source_review_scope: All47 broad_non_curadi unrecognized usable answers; no whole-cohort source certification. Includes outcome-independent puadi coverage scan of all1800 selected inputs.

rows.basis: Exact maha pujayam is parasmaipada (Dhatupradipa mahati); Lot third singular takes tu or the licensed tat alternative. mahatam is the wrong ending/pada.
Tudadi dip kshepe is inside kutadi; the non-nit/nnit ending is ngit and guna is blocked. didepitha imports guna into this exact class entry.
Divadi vrsha is in pushadi; parasmaipada aorist has ang. avarshishta uses the wrong sic/middle construction for this entry.
Exact rage shankayam is parasmaipada; Dhatupradipa ragati. Optative middle -eyatham is not licensed by the supplied citation.
Tudadi chuta chedane is a kutadi entry; the conditional sya is not nnit/nit, so ngit blocks guna. achotishyan wrongly changes u to o.
The supplied snai root has no atmanepada it marker; its root accent is not an anudatta-it suffix. Dhatupradipa snayati confirms P. asnayathah uses M.
Supplied shatha is P; Dhatupradipa shathati. -ishyante is middle rather than requested ordinary P union for this exact entry.

Kashika explicitly gives sr gatau -> asarat without a class restriction; Madhaviya restricts the ang rule to the Juhotyadi entry by association with shas. The supplied Bhvadi sr and returned asaran therefore have a genuine commentary-scope conflict; do not resolve it from VP alone.
Supplied shita anadare is P; Dhatupradipa shetati. shetavahe is middle, not the P first dual shetavah.
The a-final dhma aorist P requires sag and it before sic. adhmastam omits the resulting -sishtam material; compare the primary ayas-ishtam construction.

The optional dh->dh-retroflex after it requires an in-final preceding anga. vas is consonant-final s; a preceding inserted i alone does not satisfy the lexical condition. avasidhvam dental dh remains required.
Exact hudr is P (r-it is not an atmanepada marker); hodishiya is M. Also long medial u is not the laghu upadha entitled to guna.

Dhatupradipa treats marana/toshana/nishamana jna in the mit group as a mit prescription on janati, rather than an unequivocally independent Bhvadi lexeme. Kashika permits unprefixed janati middle for agent-directed fruit. Thus jajnjivahe cannot safely be rejected solely from the engine treating this code as Bhvadi P; exact identity/scope needs resolution.

Kashika/Nyasa explicitly distinguish trpha/trmpha: only the already nasal/anushanga entry receives the obligatory nasal extension; the nonnasal entry yields trphati. The supplied nonnasal trpha does not license trmphami.
Adadi ra dane is a P entry; root accent is not an anudatta-it marker. rasiyastam is an M benedictive and is not licensed by unspecified pada for this exact citation.

Dhatupradipa gatravinama listings associate jabh/jrbhi with jambhate and a jabhi alternative with jabhate; 7.1.61 supplies num to jabhi. The supplied jaBa~ has no anudatta-it or i-it but the same meaning. This is unresolved dictionary-identity evidence, not grounds to accept any nasal/middle replacement or reject it solely from VP.
The requested aorist first singular P requires mip->am (and the a-final sic formation). ajasi lacks that first-singular ending; it is not a licensed contraction of ajasisham.
Pish has short laghu medial i before sarvadhatuka P thematic formation, so guna e is required. pisheva incorrectly retains i.
Daip shodhane is P (Dhatupradipa dayati). dayasva is M; the lexical p-it does not confer middle.

In the periphrastic perfect, the long-vowel initial ing root takes am, an ardhadhatuka formation, with guna and subsequent e->ay before am. iyancakrath e incorrectly uses the present iyang stem instead of ayam-.
Druñ occurs before puñ, outside both primary puadi scope readings. shna weak-ending a->i does not shorten the root u. drunitah has an unlicensed short root vowel; drunitah with long u is required.

Kashika explicitly exempts sthivu (initial retroflex sh) from the otherwise general dhatvadi sh->s replacement. The returned asthivyam dentalizes the initial sh; Divadi membership does not remove this exception.
Cadi ahlade diptau has nasal i but no anudatta-it marker. The prescribed P second-dual perfect ending is athuh; c acandathe is M.

The exact long-r pF perfect weak stem has compulsory guna or optional short-r+yan, yielding papar-/papr-. Nyasa 7.4.12 explicitly says short-r blocks the u substitution. papurathuh wrongly uses labial u in this context.
Ch o chedane becomes a-final before the non-shit benedictive construction; chayat follows. cheyat substitutes e without this licensing.
The exact svana entry has no middle marker, and is treated in the P/mit group; svaneyatham is M rather than P second dual. This does not resolve unrelated svan/svanj lexical substitutions.
Ija gatikutsana has long medial i, corroborated by Dhatupradipa ijate/periphrastic ijancakre. Laghupadha guna does not turn that long vowel into e; ejishyete is the wrong stem.
Dy ai is P; dyayamahai uses the middle first-plural imperative. The unmarked public pada requires accepting licensed P/M possibilities, not arbitrary substitution of M endings.

Kashika gives a puadi-through-end-of-Kryadi reading alongside the shorter range. The visually checked Dhatupradipa printed127 footnote explicitly includes kshish among roots with short-vowel and long-vowel school readings. kshi + shna + si, with sh-conditioned hrasva and subsequent natva, yields ksh inasi. Accept exact क्षिणासि alongside canonical क्षीणासि; no school is chosen in the prompt.
Conditional is ngit; first-person final s is obligatorily deleted. amedishyamah retains the present/future first-plural visarga in a conditional form.
Primary commentary explicitly distinguishes nonnasal drpha from drmph a; only the latter licenses the obligatory nasal treatment. adrmphah imports another lexical entry into the supplied drpha.

Literal supplied SUWa with long u does not permit laghupadha guna, but Dhatupradipa has short shutha at the same Bhvadi meaning gatipratighata (shothati), which would support shothita. This unresolved entry-reading conflict should not be certified as a model error from the frozen long-vowel engine key.
Haya gatau is P (Dhatupradipa hayati). hayishyavahe is the middle first dual, unsupported for the supplied entry.
Kashika distinguishes gupha from gumpha, expressly retaining nonnasal guphati. Thus agumphishva imports the nasal entry; the nonnasal root also has ordinary laghupadha guna in this sic P formation.
Lot third-dual P takes tam and thematic a gives bindatam. bindetam introduces the middle/optative e pattern instead of the specified imperative P ending.
Maghi mandane has nasal i, not an anudatta-it marker, and is P in the supplied entry. manghedhvam is the middle optative second plural.
Sage samvarane is P; Dhatupradipa sagati in the same mit group. segimahe uses a middle ending instead of P first-plural -ima.
A-final jya takes the sag/it sic P formation. ajyastam drops the required -sishtam sequence, matching neither the specified P second dual nor a licensed variant.
Tudadi muna is before the kutadi subsection, so its short medial u undergoes guna in the it-sic construction. amunishva omits the required guna; 7.2.4 blocks vrddhi, not this guna.
Kakhe hasane is P (Dhatupradipa kakhati). akakhathah is middle second singular, unsupported by its supplied citation.
Conditional is ngit; second-plural tha is replaced with ta. adhvarishyatha retains the simple-future ending instead of the conditional ending.
The explicit sthivu exception prohibits initial sh->s dentalization. sthivyas ma begins with dental s, independently invalid even before considering the separate lengthening context.
Kashika explicitly lists trpnu/trpnoti under the shubhnadi natva prohibition. atrpnutam must keep dental n; atrpnutam with retroflex n violates this named exception.
Nyasa/Kashika explain that ir-it is one composite marker, so its i is not independently idit. Thus the supplied skhadir does not acquire num by idito num dhatoh. skhanderan improperly adds n.
Raha tyage is P (Dhatupradipa rahati), and the conditional first dual is -ava. ara hishyavahi imports the M ending.
Chuda samvarane belongs to kutadi, for which the non-nit/nnit future suffix is ngit. chodishyamah violates guna blocking for this exact entry.

The short-root branch bhri-nati is valid under the wider puadi reading (Nyasa explicitly names bhri bhaye), so root shortening alone is not an error. The returned bhrinite nevertheless uses unlicensed middle pada; source variant is भ्रिणाति, not भ्रिणीते.

limitations: Rejections adjudicate only the returned exact answer under its public entry. They do not certify the entire canonical union.
Unresolved dictionary/commentary identities remain unresolved, never silently scored as source-certified errors.
Ordinary pada rules are applied to exact visible citations; no separate pada choice was given, and all source-licensed pada possibilities must be retained.
Dhatupradipa excerpts are OCR locators; the critical optional-shortening page137 image was visually checked.
No model response, frozen key, alias policy, ledger, task membership, or shared policy was changed. Proposed additions require separate adoption and symmetric application.
